Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GreenWave Energy Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GreenWave Energy Corp.'s results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; and Elena Morales, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by our continued focus on innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. We are seeing strong demand for our renewable energy solutions across all markets.

Here are six key highlights from the quarter:

1. Exceptional overall results with revenue up 48% year-over-year to $1.45 billion, adjusted EBITDA at $425 million with 29% margins, and a record 12.8 GW backlog valued at $18 billion.

2. Favorable market trends including record global renewable additions of 510 GW year-to-date, solar dominance at 420 GW, and surging storage deployments boosting our pipeline to 18 GW.

3. Successful capital recycling through $1.2 billion in asset sales totaling 750 MW, recycling proceeds into high-return greenfield projects and maintaining strong ROIC at 11.2%.

4. Disciplined CAPEX of $1.2 billion year-to-date and flat OPEX per MW at $14,500, supporting 5.2 GW of new capacity while expanding EBITDA margins to 68%.

5. Gross margins expanding to 32.4%, up 420 basis points year-over-year, driven by vertical integration and premium product mix, with operating margins at 15.2%.

6. Supportive policy environment led by the IRA, REPowerEU, and global incentives unlocking billions in credits and accelerating our project IRRs.

Now, I will turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. We are very pleased with our financial performance in Q3. Revenue was $1.45 billion, a 48% increase year-over-year. This increase was driven by higher project commissioning and energy sales. Gross margin was 32.4%, reflecting improved cost management and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $285 million, primarily due to increased investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $210 million, or $0.78 per share. We ended the quarter with $2.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings, now raised to $5.4-5.6 billion in revenue and $1.55-1.60 billion in adjusted EBITDA.

Before diving deeper into the numbers, let me expand on some of these highlights starting with the significant market trends shaping our industry and their direct impact on GreenWave. As a leader in integrated solar PV, utility-scale BESS, and emerging green hydrogen, our results reflect both solid execution and strong macro tailwinds accelerating the energy transition. Global renewable capacity additions reached a record 510 GW year-to-date in 2024 per IRENA, up 24% from last year, with solar PV leading at 420 GW due to module prices falling to $0.22 per Wp and LCOE under $20 per MWh in sunny areas like the US Southwest and India. Wind added 75 GW, and storage hit 125 GWh, up 45% year-over-year. This expanded our project pipeline 15% to 18 GW, including 4.2 GW under construction.

In solar, bifacial modules now dominate, capturing 30-40% rear-side gains and lifting IRRs by 2-3 points, as seen in our 1.2 GW SunForge project in Texas using LONGi and Trina panels yielding 28% above nameplate. Our EPC ASPs stayed at $0.85 per Wdc thanks to tracker integration with Nextracker and AI soiling prediction cutting degradation below 0.4% annually. We've hedged 70% of 2025 volumes against polysilicon at $6 per kg. On wind, offshore growth to 30 GW is key, with our 800 MW WindWave hybrid in the UK pairing 12 MW Vestas turbines and 400 MWh BESS for EPEX SPOT revenue. A $150 million JV with Orsted targets 2 GW US offshore BESS by 2027, adding $300 million in annual ancillary revenue.

Storage deployments aim for 200 GWh in 2025, with LFP packs at $85 per kWh enabling $120 per kWh installed. Our 2.5 GWh California assets earned $45 million in CAISO payments at 92% efficiency, with 35% margins from our EMS software on $150 per MWh arbitrage. We've hedged 80% lithium exposure and tested sodium-ion. Green hydrogen electrolyzers announced 25 GW globally, with costs at $3.5 per kg; our 100 MW Australian pilot hits $2.8 per kg. We're investing $25 million in perovskite tandems for 35% efficiency.

Policy tailwinds amplify this: IRA's 45X credits at our Texas factory, 75% ITC for storage adding $200 million; REPowerEU's 600 GW target aiding our Polish pipeline; India's 500 GW goal with Rajasthan PPA at $0.03 per kWh. North America is 45% of backlog with ERCOT growth; Europe 30% with grid reforms; APAC 20%; Latin America 5%. Renewables to 35% global electricity by 2030 drives 22% revenue CAGR. We've raised FY25 guidance to $3.8-4.0 billion revenue, $950-1.05 billion EBITDA.

Turning to capital recycling, a core strategy, we divested stabilized assets post-construction to fund new development, enhancing ROIC to 11.2%. In Q3, two deals totaled 750 MW for $1.2 billion: 500 MW SunVista solar to Brookfield at 7.2% cap rate, 14.8% IRR; 250 MW Horizon Wind to BlackRock at 7.5%. Year-to-date, $2.8 billion from 1.8 GW, 85% redeployed to 5.2 GW pipeline including Southwest hybrids. US is 70% with IRA tax credits; Europe 400 MW for 450 million euros; Australia 150 MW. Net debt-to-EBITDA at 3.2x. Proceeds fund 50 MW iron-air LDES and offshore turbines. FY24 recycling guide $3.5-4.0 billion on 2.5 GW.

On CAPEX and OPEX, we spent $1.2 billion year-to-date, up 28%, guiding $1.6-1.8 billion full-year for 5.2 GW online. Solar 42% or $504 million at $0.82 per Wdc with LONGi bifacials and perovskite pilots. Wind 35% or $420 million, including $280 million Atlantic Horizon offshore at $3.2 million per MW. BESS 23% or $276 million at $145 per kWh with iron-air tests. Efficiency at $1.05 million per MW. Q4 $450 million BESS-focused. OPEX $285 million Q3, $14,500 per MW on 12.4 GW fleet, EBITDA margins 68%. O&M $137 million with AI reducing downtime 25%; SG&A $80 million at 4.2% revenue; leases $68 million. US lowest at $12k per MW. OPEX guide $380-400 million.

Gross margins hit 32.4% Q3, up 420 bps YoY and 110 bps sequentially, trailing four-quarter average 31.1% above peers. Vertical integration at 10 GW Texas TOPCon fab cut COGS to $0.23 per W, ASP $0.34 per W on Gemini bifacials at 23.5% efficiency. US 35.2% on IRA and BESS; Europe 30.8%; APAC 28.5%. TOPCon cuts degradation to 0.4%, AI stringing saves 1.2%. Operating margins 15.2%, up 310 bps, OpEx 17.2% with R&D 4.2% on HJT. US 17.8%, Europe 13.5%. Q3 guide 33-34%, FY 32.5-33.5%; op margins 15.5-16.5%.

On policy, IRA extends ITC to 70% stacked, adding $1.2 billion Q3 incentives, 45% US solar surge. FERC 2222 mandates storage. Europe RED III to 45%, 8 GW German auctions at 50 euros per MWh, 450 million euros Dutch grants. Australia LSIL, India PLI. Global carbon pricing covers 24%, driving PPAs. Risks like permitting delays, but positioned for 20% EBITDA uplift.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Patel for an update on our project pipeline.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Our project pipeline continues to grow, with 18 GW of projects under development. We are making good progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, including 1.2 GW hybrids in the Southwest. We are also actively exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships, like our recent BayWa r.e. deal and Orsted JV.

Next, Dr. Raj Singh will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Raj Singh:
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to developing and deploying innovative technologies that improve the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems. We are making significant progress on our research and development efforts, including advanced solar panel technologies like perovskite tandems targeting 35% efficiency, energy storage solutions such as iron-air LDES for 100-hour discharge, and smart grid technologies with AI-driven EMS. The development of our proprietary NovaOptix AI platform is expected to have a transformative impact on our future projects, delivering 5% yield uplifts, 18% less downtime, and 200 bps higher IRRs through predictive O&M and arbitrage optimization. We believe that these technologies will play a critical role in accelerating the transition to a clean energy future.

And now, Elena Morales will provide an update on our sustainability efforts.

Elena Morales:
Thank you, Dr. Singh. We are committed to operating our business in a sustainable manner and minimizing our environmental impact. We have set ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions to net-zero Scope 1 and 2 by 2028 per SBTi, improving our energy efficiency across the portfolio, and promoting responsible resource management including blade recycling and water use in deserts. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability, such as RE100 compliance and REBA certification. We believe that sustainability is not only the right thing to do but also makes good business sense, enhancing premiums and stakeholder trust.

I'll now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Elena. In closing, we are confident that GreenWave Energy Corp. is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register for a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Doe:
Can you provide more details on the regulatory environment for renewable energy projects in your key markets?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks for the question, John. The regulatory landscape remains highly supportive. In the US, the IRA continues to deliver with ITC stackers up to 70%, driving 45% solar growth and storage mandates under FERC 2222—our SunForge BESS exemplifies this with full adders. We're pushing for FAST-41 reforms to cut NEPA delays from 4.5 years. In Europe, REPowerEU and RED III target 45% renewables, with German auctions at 50 euros per MWh and Dutch Hydrogen Bank subsidies for our IJmuiden project. UK CfD AR6 at 44 pounds per MWh aids offshore. APAC sees Australia's CIS fast-tracking hybrids and India's RTC RE mandates. Globally, carbon pricing and CBAM favor us, though election risks and permitting persist—we model 20% EBITDA uplift through diversification.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jane Smith:
How is the company addressing the challenges of energy storage integration with your renewable energy projects?

Dr. Raj Singh:
Great question, Jane. Storage is pivotal for grid stability amid 2 TW US queues. Deployments hit 125 GWh this year, targeting 200 GWh next, with LFP at $85 per kWh pack-level. Our 2.5 GWh California fleet at 92% efficiency earned $45 million via CAISO, 35% margins on EMS arbitrage at $150 per MWh peaks. Challenges like lithium at $12k per tonne—we've hedged 80% and shifted 30% to sodium-ion. Hybrids like WindWave integrate 400 MWh BESS for curtailment monetization. Long-duration iron-air pilots with Form Energy offer 100-hour discharge at half cost. IRA 75% ITC and NEM 3.0 mandates accelerate this; our Nevada gigafactory ramps to 10 GWh for firming.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
What are your expectations for the long-term growth of the renewable energy market?

Sarah Thompson:
Mike, we're bullish. IEA sees renewables at 35% global electricity by 2030 per STEPS, with $2 trillion annual investments outpacing fossils. Capacity triples to 12% share now jumping via 510 GW 2024 adds. Solar to dominate, wind offshore accelerates, storage to 50 GW US by 2030. Policies like IRA, REPowerEU, India's 500 GW drive $1.7 trillion capex needs. Our 22% revenue CAGR to 2027, 25 GW awards ahead, leverages hybrids and $28 billion backlog. Challenges like interconnection delays met by $2.5 billion liquidity, 85% contracted assets.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, there appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for any closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in GreenWave Energy Corp. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
